create.title: Literal divisor-progressive half-shifted alias reduction
create.statement_tex: For every persistent literal j=1 balanced block, expand the second low-gcd mask over odd d|h',k', write h'=h+2s=d(ell_d+2t) with s=s_d+dt and h+2s_d=d ell_d, and Poisson-sum in t. The literal aliases are mu=1/2-m in Z+1/2 and lambda=mu/d, with dL^3 active lifts, stationary amplitude (dL)^(-1), and residue phase s_d(1/2-lambda). The stationary point is x=Xk'/lambda^2 and the phase is R sqrt(hk)-Xk'/(2lambda)-lambda h/2+s_d(1/2-lambda)=-h(lambda-R sqrt(k/h))^2/(2lambda)-Xq/(2lambda)+s_d(1/2-lambda). The two gates are exactly rho=[hk'/lambda^2](lambda^2-lambda_0^2) and Delta=[hk/lambda^2](lambda_r^2-lambda^2). Finite Poisson on the literal integer runs, with incomplete Fresnel transitions and signed boundary tails retained, has aggregate boundary, nonstationary, support-crossing, and stationary-remainder cost O_epsilon(L^3X^epsilon). Hence R_B^osc=K_B-M_B^(0)+O_epsilon(L^3X^epsilon), where K_B is the complete signed lifted kernel and the phase-free owner M_B^(0) is used once. The estimate |K_B^bulk|<<L^3X^epsilon remains open.
create.next_action: Use only the complete signed (d,mu,h,k,v) kernel with both gates, actual amplitudes, lift phases, and endpoint packages. Do not merge rational lifts or take aliaswise absolute values.

create.title: One-alias reciprocal counting, spacing, and second-B-process self-return
create.statement_tex: On the literal odd-d divisor progression there are dL^3 aliases of amplitude (dL)^(-1). Aliaswise l1 has L^5 global capacity at d=1, while square mass L/d only preserves primal energy. Writing k'=dv gives reciprocal frequency Xd^2/(2mu); optimal near-hyperbola divisor counting repays only the first-transform loss and returns L^4 global capacity. N_d=dL^3 frequencies sampled Q_d=L/d times force clusters of size d^2L^2, d^3L^5 ordered close pairs, and coefficient-uniform large-sieve constant at least N_d. A second B-process in mu has phase -dR sqrt(v(ell_d+2n)), exactly restores h'=d(ell_d+2n), the character, reciprocal Jacobian, and original L/d range. The proposed positive row energy is a stronger replicated Gram that would force the full scalar sum to be O(L), not merely O(L^(3/2)). Thus aliaswise triangles, reciprocal-v counting alone, spacing-only large sieves followed by outer norms, a second B-process, and row-energy equivalence cannot certify the missing factor L. This is a method obstruction, not a lower bound for the actual remainder or a disproof of BAL.
create.next_action: Do not repeat one-alias reciprocal counting, coefficient-blind spacing-only large sieve, positive row Gram, or a second one-variable B-process. Revisit BAL only with a new noninvertible signed joint-kernel theorem.

reject.reason: After expanding the second gcd mask, s lies on odd-d progressions and the literal lattice is lambda=(1/2-m)/d with dL^3 lifts, amplitude (dL)^(-1), and a residue phase. The clean half-integer grid is only the d=1 bulk model.
Different representations lambda=mu/d carry different gamma_d coefficients, congruence data, and residue phases. Reducing the fraction and merging lifts changes the literal sum.
There are dL^3 stationary aliases of size (dL)^(-1). At d=1 aliaswise l1 has global L^5 capacity, one factor worse than the L^4 primal capacity and two factors above the L^3 target.
The literal frequency is Xd^2/(2mu). Optimal product-window counting and dyadic geometric-sum bounds only repay the first Poisson inflation and return L^4 global capacity.
N_d=dL^3 frequencies sampled Q_d=L/d times force d^2L^2-sized clusters and a coefficient-uniform large-sieve constant at least N_d. The diagonal exhausts the available energy before outer norms.
The mu B-process exactly returns the original h'=d(ell_d+2n), k'=dv progression, character, reciprocal Jacobian, Fresnel normalization, and L/d range. Two transforms are involutive.

The double-far rows are S_B minus target-safe corridors. An L^4 row-energy bound would force |S_B|<<L, stronger than the L^(3/2) scalar scale; it is a distinct nearly replicated Gram and is false coefficient-uniformly.

The stated theorem has separated phase and coefficient hypotheses plus parameter conditions not matched by the divisor-dependent lattices, coupled gcd/slanted symbols, residue phases, pair-dependent gates, and boundary kernels. Its abstract spacing energies remain unproved here.
